issuing_authority: Firstsource Solutions Limited (Information Risk Management; approved by SVP - IRM)
geo_constraints: Work on Firstsource-owned devices or networks on behalf of Firstsource and its clients

locale_context.regulation: Self-regulation · mandatory internal policy under the information-security management system, with disciplinary sanctions
locale_context.culture: Client-service outsourcing context: strong emphasis on client data confidentiality, approved-tool lists and contractual protections, with EU AI Act deployer duties copied in for client work in regulated markets.

key_dates.event: Date printed in the page footer of this copy

covered_entities: third-party individuals using AI on Firstsource devices or networks
AI deployers and developers within Firstsource
covered_systems: generative AI, predictive AI and conversational intelligence
external/third-party and internally built AI tools
high-risk AI systems (EU AI Act sense)
exceptions: Exceptions to be sought from the Chief Digital and AI Officer and Head of Enterprise Transformation
conditions: Only AI tools vetted by the AICoE and approved by the Chief Digital and AI Officer, Head – Enterprise Transformation and CIO may be used, via company-provided accounts
objective: Establish guidelines and best practices for the safe, responsible and ethical use and development of AI and generative AI within Firstsource, protecting company and client data and ensuring legal compliance.

related_policies.policy: Firstsource Incident Management policy and Data Privacy policies
Artificial Intelligence Disclosure (AID) Framework (cited by the document as 'of 2012')

conflict_rule: All AI tools and processes must comply with applicable laws, regulations and industry standards; exceptions only with approval of the Chief Digital and AI Officer and Head of Enterprise Transformation.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/firstsource.pdf). Policy v1.0, ref PL-ISMS-ENT-016, released 8 July 2024 (header: 'July, 2024'), review date January 2025, next review January 2026; page footers carry 11 March 2025 (likely print/copy date). Mandatory for employees, contractors and third parties, with disciplinary action up to dismissal (binding=false: corporate policy, not law). The document is marked 'Firstsource RESTRICTED' (authorization list: employees, vendors, current/prospective clients); it is public only through the asago repository, so whether Firstsource intended publication is uncertain. Section 13 copies EU AI Act Article 26 deployer obligations nearly word for word. The document cites an 'Artificial Intelligence Disclosure (AID) Framework of 2012' with an example naming ChatGPT v.4o; the year appears to be an error in the source and is reproduced as cited. Whether a newer version exists is unknown. Extraction was clean apart from a broken word ('co mpliance').

clauses.original_text: Employees must safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company information always. Company information relating to Firstsource, its clients or associated organizations and individuals, or information that could reasonably be used to identify Firstsource or its client(s), or a commercially sensitive course of action should never be entered into generative AI technology without the express permission of the client and client lead.
clauses.object: company, client and commercially sensitive information
clauses.requirement: no company or client information into generative AI without express permission
clauses.exception: with the express permission of the client and client lead
clauses.purpose: protect confidentiality of company and client information
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened. Reinforced by 8.2 Data Guardrails (no sensitive personal data, restricted data or credentials) and 8.3.

clauses.original_text: Employees must always verify data produced via generative AI. It should never be used as a single source of the truth and only to supplement additional research or writing methods.
clauses.requirement: verify GenAI output and never treat it as a single source of truth
clauses.affected_asset: quality and accuracy of work product
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened. Repeated in 8.1 Guidelines (human review for accuracy, bias, IP and hallucinations).

clauses.original_text: Employees must not use AI programs to create or disseminate malicious software or engage in hacking or other unauthorized activities. Don’t Use AI to Spread Misinformation or Disinformation
clauses.action: use AI to create malware, hack or spread misinformation
clauses.requirement: no malicious, hacking or disinformation uses of AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened. Two consecutive bullets of the Don’ts list; other Don’ts include not replacing human judgment in critical decisions and not manipulating or exploiting vulnerable groups.

clauses.original_text: Do not use GenAI tools to make or help you make employment decisions about applicants or employees, including recruitment, hiring, retention, promotions, transfers, performance monitoring, discipline, demotion, or terminations.
clauses.action: use GenAI tools for employment decisions
clauses.object: employment decisions about applicants or employees
clauses.purpose: fair treatment of applicants and employees
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened.

clauses.section: 8.4 AI-Generated Output Guardrails – a. AI Only Responses
clauses.original_text: If an AI feature shall directly present a response to customers or third parties without human review or intervention, you must disclose to the customer that they are: Engaging solely with an AI. Responsible for checking it for accuracy.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI-only interaction and the customer's responsibility to check accuracy
clauses.condition: where an AI feature responds without human review or intervention
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened. The sub-bullets are interleaved in the PDF with other bullets (sensitive topics need human review; customer responsible for checking for bias; sample disclaimer text); quoted here as the opening sentence plus its first two sub-bullets.

clauses.original_text: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use and, where relevant, inform providers in accordance with Article 72 EU Artificial Intelligence Act. Where deployers have reason to consider that the use of the high-risk AI system in accordance with the instructions may result in that AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) EU Artificial Intelligence Act, they shall, without undue delay, inform the provider or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authority, and shall suspend the use of that system.
clauses.recipient: providers, distributors and market surveillance authorities
clauses.requirement: monitor high-risk AI, report risks and suspend use
clauses.condition: where use may result in a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) EU AI Act
clauses.affected_asset: persons affected by high-risk AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from the asago copy (firstsource.pdf); line breaks collapsed and bullets flattened. Copies EU AI Act Article 26(5) almost verbatim. Section 13 also requires log retention of at least six months and assigning competent human oversight.
